00212 is 10 mg/kg every 14 days; 00215 is 15 mg/kg every 21 days. Do not merge their current source eligibility or partner schedules.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Exemestane lowers oestrogen production while everolimus blocks an intracellular growth pathway that can contribute to endocrine resistance. The aim in this setting is to control cancer and delay progression.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Postmenopausal HR-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Everolimus: Everolimus binds the intracellular protein FKBP12; this complex inhibits mTORC1, affecting protein synthesis and growth signalling. This pathway can support endocrine resistance, which explains pairing it with an oestrogen-lowering medicine. The same pathway operates in normal tissues, contributing to mouth ulcers, infection risk and metabolic changes. Exemestane: After menopause, aromatase in tissues converts androgen precursors into oestrogen. Exemestane is an irreversible aromatase inhibitor that reduces this supply to hormone-sensitive cancer cells. It does not directly switch off functioning ovaries; the menopausal indication must be confirmed.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Usual starting doses are everolimus 10 mg once daily and exemestane 25 mg once daily; use the doses on your prescription. Both tablets are taken every day continuously. There is no planned rest week. Review benefit and tolerability over time; there is no fixed adjuvant completion date.
key_points: Usual starting doses are everolimus 10 mg once daily and exemestane 25 mg once daily; use the doses on your prescription. Both tablets are taken every day continuously. There is no planned rest week. Review benefit and tolerability over time; there is no fixed adjuvant completion date.
Continue while beneficial and tolerated; review each medicine separately if everolimus is held.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Palbociclib slows cell-cycle progression while the hormone partner reduces oestrogen signalling. The aim in this advanced-disease pathway is cancer control, with treatment and response reviewed over time.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Palbociclib: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division. Your endocrine partner: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant acts at the oestrogen receptor. These are alternative partners here, not an instruction to take both. The partner’s dose, monitoring and injection or tablet schedule must be confirmed.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The usual palbociclib starting dose is 125 mg once daily; a lower dose may be prescribed. Palbociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, then paused on Days 22–28 of each 28-day cycle. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily, or fulvestrant follows its injection schedule. Ovarian suppression has its own plan when required.
key_points: The usual palbociclib starting dose is 125 mg once daily; a lower dose may be prescribed. Palbociclib is taken once daily on Days 1–21, then paused on Days 22–28 of each 28-day cycle. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily, or fulvestrant follows its injection schedule. Ovarian suppression has its own plan when required.
Repeat while beneficial and tolerated. The planned week off concerns palbociclib, not automatically the endocrine partner.
NCCP describes capsules with food; current product information also has tablets that may be taken with or without food. Confirm formulation.

AI or fulvestrant: An aromatase inhibitor (AI) lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant blocks and reduces oestrogen receptors. These are alternative endocrine partners, selected by the team. Ovarian suppression is needed in pre/perimenopausal patients.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The usual metastatic starting dose is ribociclib 600 mg once daily on Days 1–21 followed by Days 22–28 off. Continue the prescribed AI daily or fulvestrant on its own injection schedule; add ovarian suppression when indicated. Continue while beneficial and tolerated.
key_points: The usual metastatic starting dose is ribociclib 600 mg once daily on Days 1–21 followed by Days 22–28 off. Continue the prescribed AI daily or fulvestrant on its own injection schedule; add ovarian suppression when indicated. Continue while beneficial and tolerated.
There is no fixed three-year stop in this metastatic regimen; the team reviews response, side effects and the next treatment decision.
Ribociclib is not recommended with tamoxifen; do not present all endocrine partners as interchangeable.

Metastatic QT restart guidance differs from the early-breast schedule and differs between current NCCP and SmPC in some branches; keep specialist review rather than calculate an automatic restart dose.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: For eligible high-risk node-positive early breast cancer, adding abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence after surgery.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer · adjuvant
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Abemaciclib: Abemaciclib inhibits CDK4 and CDK6 proteins. These proteins help cells move towards division. It is combined with endocrine treatment to reduce recurrence risk in eligible high-risk early breast cancer. Your endocrine treatment: The chosen endocrine medicine either reduces oestrogen production or blocks its action. An aromatase inhibitor may need ovarian suppression before menopause. The exact drug and duration are prescribed separately.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The usual abemaciclib starting dose is 150 mg twice daily; a lower dose or altered schedule may be prescribed. Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously for up to two years with endocrine therapy, unless recurrence or unacceptable toxicity requires an earlier change. A four-week dispensing block is not a rest cycle. Endocrine treatment normally continues beyond abemaciclib.
key_points: The usual abemaciclib starting dose is 150 mg twice daily; a lower dose or altered schedule may be prescribed. Abemaciclib is taken twice daily continuously for up to two years with endocrine therapy, unless recurrence or unacceptable toxicity requires an earlier change. A four-week dispensing block is not a rest cycle. Endocrine treatment normally continues beyond abemaciclib.
At completion of the planned two-year abemaciclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.
Prior VTE is a caution; review endocrine-partner clot risk, particularly tamoxifen.
Diarrhoea often starts early; agree access to antidiarrhoeal treatment before the first dose.
New respiratory symptoms need assessment for ILD/pneumonitis, infection or thrombosis.

evidence_at_a_glance.population: 5,637 patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative, node-positive high-risk early breast cancer; intention-to-treat trial population. NCCP00619 uses its specified clinicopathological high-risk criteria.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Two years of abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy versus endocrine therapy alone; endocrine therapy planned for at least five years.
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Adjuvant recurrence prevention after definitive surgery. Do not extend to node-negative disease or replace NCCP timing and high-risk criteria with the broader trial label.
evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: The primary OS analysis met the prespecified significance boundary; invasive and distant recurrence benefits persisted after the two-year abemaciclib course.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer, within the NCCP prior-treatment criteria
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Trastuzumab deruxtecan delivers a topoisomerase-I-inhibiting payload through HER2 binding to control selected advanced breast cancer. HER2-positive and HER2-low indications have separate prior-treatment criteria.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive or HER2-low breast cancer, within the NCCP prior-treatment criteria
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu): Enhertu links an antibody that recognises HER2 with deruxtecan, a cell-killing medicine. After uptake into the cell, the payload inhibits topoisomerase I and interferes with DNA replication. The released payload can also affect nearby tumour cells. This targeting does not spare every healthy cell, which is why blood counts, nausea, lungs and heart function still need attention.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: One infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle. The next infusion is normally three weeks later. A delayed appointment is rescheduled by the team; patients do not calculate catch-up doses.
key_points: NCCP00776a: unresectable/metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after at least one anti-HER2 regimen. NCCP00776b: unresectable/metastatic HER2-low breast cancer after chemotherapy for metastatic disease, or recurrence during or within six months after adjuvant chemotherapy.
Usual starting dose 5.4 mg/kg intravenously on Day 1 every 21 days; prescribed reductions are 4.4 then 3.2 mg/kg

Treatment continues while it controls the cancer and side effects remain acceptable. This advanced-disease regimen has no automatic one-year completion date. A good scan does not by itself instruct a treatment break.

Enhertu is different from trastuzumab and trastuzumab emtansine (Kadcyla); they are not interchangeable. Carry the supplied Enhertu lung-safety alert card. The team may pause treatment while investigating suspected lung inflammation; symptomatic drug-related ILD requires permanent discontinuation under the protocol.

NCCP specifies echo/MUGA before treatment and every 12 weeks. With uninterrupted three-week cycles, week 12 is approximately before cycle 5 and week 24 before cycle 9. Delays do not reset the elapsed-time monitoring clock. Signs of cardiac impairment can require 4–8-weekly checks; an abnormal result meeting the treatment-hold criteria requires repeat assessment within three weeks.
Enhertu alone does not require a routine bone-density scan schedule. DEXA, bone medicines or bone scans are added for another treatment, fracture risk, symptoms or disease assessment when indicated.
NCCP00776v3b remains the eligibility anchor despite broader EMA indications. Do not silently add first-line pertuzumab combinations, HER2-ultralow, other tissue sites or earlier-line HER2-low use.
Every12-week echo is an elapsed-time interval; cycle5/9 mapping assumes uninterrupted21-day dosing. New dysfunction changes the interval and treatment decision.
Grade1 ILD restart needs complete Grade0 resolution; ≤28days permits the same dose and >28days a reduction. Symptomatic Grade≥2 ILD requires permanent discontinuation and prompt corticosteroids.

NCCP expects no dose adjustment in severe renal impairment/dialysis; EMA says requirements cannot be determined. Moderate hepatic impairment also has a source-language difference. The engine flags specialist/pharmacy reconciliation rather than inventing a numeric dose.
Neither current NCCP nor the retrieved EMA SmPC supplies a platelet-specific dose ladder. FBC review remains mandatory; US-label thrombocytopenia instructions are not silently substituted.
NCCP eligibility says age>18 while the indication and EMA say adults. The age18 boundary is flagged for clinical/pharmacy interpretation.
Routine prophylactic steroids for antiemesis and high-dose treatment for ILD serve different purposes; patient information must not imply self-starting ILD steroids.

Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. Less frequent monitoring may suit indolent disease. New symptoms or suspected progression need earlier assessment. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not an automatic three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Previously treated unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Sacituzumab govitecan targets Trop-2 to deliver the topoisomerase-I inhibitor SN-38, aiming to control previously treated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Previously treated unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy): The antibody component recognises Trop-2 on cancer cells. Its linked SN-38 payload interferes with topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in managing DNA during copying, which can damage dividing cells. Healthy tissues can also be affected, particularly blood-forming cells and the gut; being antibody-directed does not mean it is free of chemotherapy-type effects.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Two treatment visits in each three-week cycle: Day 1, then Day 8. There is no planned infusion on Day 15. The next cycle starts after Day 21 if the team confirms it is appropriate.
key_points: NCCP00794a covers adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease. The NCCP entry specifies ECOG 0–1. Broader European licensed indications must be checked separately against the applicable Irish regimen and reimbursement pathway.
10 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; prescribed reductions may apply
Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable. There is no fixed number of cycles; the oncology team reviews benefit, scans and tolerability.

Blood-count rules differ between Day 1 and Day 8. Known reduced UGT1A1 activity may increase side effects, but routine genotype testing is not required by the EU product information. Important differences between the NCCP and current EU dose-modification wording are flagged for Consultant and oncology-pharmacy review; patients should never change the dose themselves.
An ECG is used when clinically indicated. Sacituzumab alone does not require a routine echocardiogram schedule. Cardiac symptoms or other medicines may change the plan.
A routine DXA scan is not a sacituzumab-specific requirement. Bone health, bone metastases and any bone-strengthening treatment need their own individual plan.

NCCP00794a is later-line unresectable/metastatic TNBC. Do not import current EU HR-positive, first-line or pembrolizumab-combination indications without the appropriate separate NCCP/reimbursement mapping.
Day 1 ANC threshold is ≥1.5 ×10⁹/L; Day 8 is ≥1.0 ×10⁹/L. An isolated ANC <1.0 can trigger a hold without a day; 1.0–<1.5 requires day context rather than a false clearance.

NCCP high-emetic-risk prophylaxis must cover BOTH Day 1 and Day 8. The suggested dexamethasone 12 mg infusion premedicine also provides antiemetic cover; reconcile with the selected high-risk script to prevent duplication.

NCCP suggested infusion premedicines: paracetamol 1 g PO 60 minutes beforehand; chlorphenamine 10 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV and dexamethasone 12 mg PO 30 minutes beforehand. Product availability, contraindications and local prescriptions must be checked.

Primary G-CSF should be considered from cycle 1 for increased-risk patients in the current EU SmPC. Product and timing must account for Day 1 and Day 8; do not automatically generate a single generic pegfilgrastim date.

NCCP advises considering a lower initial dose for known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity and possible escalation based on cycle-1 tolerance, but gives no fixed starting reduction. The EU SmPC recommends close monitoring and does not require routine genotype testing when status is unknown. Do not re-escalate a dose previously reduced because of adverse reactions.

NCCP Table 1 repeats 25% dose reduction at the second severe non-neutropenic event, whereas the current EU SmPC gives a 10→7.5→5 mg/kg ladder. The second-event output requires Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation and suppresses automatic numeric dosing.

NCCP Table 2 predicts no renal/hepatic adjustment across broad impairment bands. EU SmPC advises avoiding use when bilirubin >1.5×ULN or AST/ALT >3×ULN without liver metastases or >5×ULN with metastases, and notes absent severe/end-stage renal data. These differences are explicit in the assessment output.

NCCP contains >48-hour and >3-week toxicity-duration rules that differ from the current EU algorithm. Persisting severe toxicity must not be treated by merely calculating a reduced dose; recovery and source reconciliation are required.

NCCP's high-dose loperamide schedule is 4 mg initially then 2 mg every two hours, continued 12 hours after the last liquid stool and never beyond 48 consecutive hours at these doses because of ileus risk. The patient-facing page should direct to an individually prescribed local oncology plan rather than print an unsupervised automatic prescription. Assess infectious causes, fever, blood, severe pain and dehydration promptly.

ongoing: An ECG is used when clinically indicated. Sacituzumab alone does not require a routine echocardiogram schedule. Cardiac symptoms or other medicines may change the plan.

Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. Less frequent monitoring may suit indolent disease. New symptoms or suspected progression need earlier assessment. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not an automatic three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

If informative, particularly when elevated at baseline or disease is not readily measurable, tumour markers may supplement clinical assessment and imaging. A marker rise alone should not trigger a treatment change. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

urgent_review_signals: Contact the oncology service immediately for fever, shivering or feeling acutely unwell; significant diarrhoea, inability to keep fluids down, dizziness, very little urine, or abdominal pain. Do not wait for the next treatment visit. During an infusion, tell staff immediately about breathing difficulty, swelling, rash, chest discomfort or faintness. Use the emergency service for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or other life-threatening symptoms.

The team chooses suitable intravenous access. A port is not automatically required and this regimen has no take-home pump. If you already have a port, staff access and flush it according to local policy; report pain, redness or swelling.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Advanced / metastatic · previously treated HER2-positive breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Tucatinib inhibits intracellular HER2 signalling, trastuzumab binds extracellular HER2, and capecitabine supplies fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy. The combination aims to control previously treated HER2-positive advanced disease.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced / metastatic · previously treated HER2-positive breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Tucatinib reduces signalling from the internal part of HER2. It works alongside trastuzumab and capecitabine, which act in different ways. Its tablet schedule continues through the capecitabine break. The body converts capecitabine into fluorouracil, which disrupts DNA and RNA processes needed for cell growth. Tablets are active chemotherapy; taking them at home still requires a clear monitoring and interruption plan. Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Tucatinib twice daily every day; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14 then off on Days 15–21; trastuzumab every 21 days by IV infusion or a locally approved under-the-skin injection. Continue while beneficial and tolerated, with clinician-approved changes.
key_points: Tumour markers, if useful, supplement symptoms and imaging. They must not alone decide whether treatment is working or should change.
Brain metastases were included in HER2CLIMB, but this does not set a universal brain MRI interval. Confirm the individual CNS imaging / radiotherapy plan.
Tucatinib can raise creatinine through transporter effects. Assess true renal function and dehydration before adjusting capecitabine; do not dismiss a rise automatically.
The current NCCP regimen includes an alternative locally approved SC trastuzumab schedule. Record route before applying dose or missed-dose advice.
Capecitabine DPD, renal and diarrhoea rules are not tucatinib rules; do not apply a single blanket percentage reduction to all components.

The team confirms blood results, side effects and the next prescription. Never double a missed dose or restart held treatment without advice.

Trastuzumab every three weeks with staff observation. IV treatment may use a cannula, PICC or port; the locally approved SC alternative uses an injection under the skin; no routine take-home infusion pump.

Your team confirms IV infusion or the locally approved under-the-skin injection. The visit length, observation and missed-dose instructions differ; ask before switching. The injection has no loading dose.

IV: first infusion 90 minutes then 30 minutes if tolerated; observe at least 6 hours from first infusion start and 2 hours from subsequent starts unless locally documented otherwise.
SC: alternate thighs, avoid unsuitable skin; observe 30 minutes after first and 15 minutes after later injections.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Docetaxel is an active taxane option for advanced breast cancer when chemotherapy is appropriate. Select 75 mg/m² according to prior treatment, organ function, neuropathy, marrow reserve, expected benefit and tolerability.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Source-defined breast, lung, gastric, gynaecological and castration-sensitive prostate cancer (including high-risk nonmetastatic prostate disease)

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Germline BRCA1/2-associated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Olaparib exploits impaired homologous-recombination repair in BRCA-associated cancer. A one-year adjuvant course reduces invasive recurrence and improves survival in selected high-risk HER2-negative early breast disease after chemotherapy and local therapy.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Germline BRCA1/2-associated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Olaparib (Lynparza): BRCA1 and BRCA2 help cells repair breaks in DNA. Some cancers with these changes rely more heavily on other repair routes. Olaparib inhibits PARP activity and traps PARP on DNA, making it harder for those cancer cells to survive DNA damage. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which is why regular blood counts matter.

key_points: High risk:TNBC residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy or node-positive/≥2 cm after adjuvant chemotherapy; HR-positive disease requires residual disease with CPS+EG≥3 after neoadjuvant therapy or≥4 positive nodes after adjuvant chemotherapy. Ideally start within 12 weeks of the last surgery, chemotherapy or radiation.

FBC, renal and liver profile every 4 weeks throughout the 12-month breast course; earlier/additional tests for symptoms or abnormal results. Review adherence, tablet supply, nausea, fatigue and all medicines.

No routine olaparib-specific ECG, echo or DXA; follow separate previous/ongoing treatment risks. Breast surveillance continues after olaparib, without automatic asymptomatic CT or tumour-marker scheduling.

Do not extend to BRCA variants of uncertain significance, all HER2-negative cancers, concurrent radiation or the other 00588 organ-specific indications. This update does not lengthen the one-year breast course.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Take olaparib tablets morning and evening every day. There is no planned week off. Blood-review appointments are usually every four weeks during this one-year breast course.
route_and_duration: Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily continuously, with source renal/toxicity/interaction adjustments. Tablets are not interchangeable with capsules. Breast duration:one year or earlier recurrence/unacceptable toxicity.
practical_workflow: Olaparib follows the chemotherapy and local-treatment plan. In OlympiA, surgery and any indicated radiotherapy were completed before olaparib, with at least a two-week gap after local treatment. NCCP advises starting ideally within twelve weeks of the last surgery, chemotherapy or radiation; your team sets the start.

For hormone receptor-positive disease, the prescribed hormone treatment can continue alongside olaparib and often continues after the one-year olaparib course. Its injections, tablets and bone checks keep their own schedule.

Choose consistent morning and evening times and check the strength and number of tablets on each new prescription. Keep a sufficient supply before weekends or holidays. No infusion pump or port is needed for olaparib itself.
The oncology team decides when and at what dose to restart after blood recovery or symptom improvement. Do not calculate a catch-up dose or restart automatically because a calendar month has passed.

Agree the stop date and ongoing breast follow-up. Endocrine treatment and breast surveillance may continue. Report persistent unexplained fatigue, infections, bruising or breathlessness even after olaparib finishes.
observation_and_access: Oral treatment with no infusion access; arrange repeat supplies and blood-review appointments.

regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Panitumumab: Panitumumab attaches to EGFR, a receptor on the outside of cells. This can interrupt signals that help some bowel cancers grow. A tumour RAS test helps identify whether this approach is suitable. EGFR also supports healthy skin, which explains why skin and nail changes need attention. Oxaliplatin: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: A 14-day cycle: panitumumab, oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil start on Day 1, followed by a fluorouracil pump lasting about 46 hours. Arrange disconnection around Day 3. Continue according to benefit and tolerance.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1 immune signalling; pemetrexed inhibits folate-dependent nucleotide synthesis and carboplatin damages DNA. The planned maintenance phase removes carboplatin while retaining pembrolizumab and pemetrexed.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: PD-1 is a control switch on T cells, a type of immune cell. When it connects with PD-L1 or PD-L2, the T cell receives a signal to reduce its activity. Some cancers use this pathway to escape immune attack. Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, helping T cells recognise and attack the cancer. It does not directly poison cancer cells like chemotherapy. Releasing this brake can also allow immune cells to attack healthy organs, which explains the different side-effect pattern and why symptoms can appear after treatment stops. Pemetrexed: Pemetrexed is an antifolate: it blocks several enzymes that cells use to turn folate-dependent materials into DNA and RNA building blocks. With fewer building blocks, cancer cells have more difficulty copying their genetic instructions and dividing. Healthy rapidly renewing tissues, including bone marrow and the mouth lining, can also be affected. That helps explain low blood counts and mouth soreness. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce toxicity; they are part of the treatment, not supplements to omit because the drug is an antifolate. Carboplatin: Carboplatin is a platinum-containing chemotherapy. Inside cells, it forms chemical attachments to DNA, including links that stop DNA strands working normally. This disrupts copying and repair and can lead to cell death. Healthy cells can also be injured, especially blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. The kidneys help remove carboplatin, so kidney function is used to calculate the dose. AUC 5 describes a target drug exposure over time; it is not a fixed dose of 5 mg.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: EGFR blockade is combined with the irinotecan/fluorouracil/folinic-acid FOLFIRI backbone to control selected metastatic colorectal cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced / metastatic colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cetuximab: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care. Irinotecan: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. Day 1 FOLFIRI includes irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat the reference cycle every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.

regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced / metastatic colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cetuximab: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care. Oxaliplatin: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. FOLFOX4 starts on Day 1: oxaliplatin, folinic acid and fluorouracil bolus, followed by a 22-hour fluorouracil infusion. Day 2 includes folinic acid, another fluorouracil bolus and a second 22-hour infusion; finish around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: EGFR blockade is combined with the oxaliplatin/fluorouracil/folinic-acid FOLFOX backbone to control selected metastatic colorectal cancer.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced / metastatic colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cetuximab: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care. Oxaliplatin: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 start on Day 1, followed by one 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable. No weekly Day 8 cetuximab is scheduled.
key_points: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 start on Day 1, followed by one 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable. No weekly Day 8 cetuximab is scheduled.
Metastatic colorectal cancer with validated extended RAS-wild-type status. The NCCP document retains older KRAS wording; the current Erbitux SmPC requires extended RAS testing.
Indirect for both schedule and backbone: OPUS used weekly cetuximab with FOLFOX4, not fortnightly cetuximab with modified FOLFOX6. Do not relabel OPUS results as an exact 00733 trial.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: FOLFOX-4 may be given after surgery for stage II or III colon cancer, or for colorectal cancer that has spread. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected. Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This combination treats metastatic or unresectable colorectal cancer when an irinotecan- or oxaliplatin-based combination is unsuitable. Its aims may include cancer control, symptom relief and longer survival.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: After you swallow capecitabine, your body changes it into fluorouracil. This interferes with the DNA and RNA processes cells use to grow. Normal cells can also be affected, which helps explain mouth soreness, bowel symptoms and changes in blood counts. Bevacizumab binds VEGF, a signal that helps blood vessels grow. Blocking it can restrict the blood supply supporting a tumour. It also affects normal blood vessels and healing, which is why blood pressure, urine and planned procedures matter.

route_and_duration: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily on Days 1–14 every 21 days. Bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV Day 1; initial 90 minutes, then 60/30 if tolerated.
practical_workflow: Confirm the aim, likely course length, blood-test arrangements and a working urgent contact number. DPD testing is required before starting the fluoropyrimidine unless already completed.

Use the prescribed morning and evening dose within 30 minutes after food on the agreed treatment days. Do not make up a missed or vomited dose. Follow the team’s hold instructions for significant diarrhoea, mouth soreness or painful hands and feet, and contact them promptly.
Ask the unit to confirm the new treatment and blood-test dates. Re-anchor supportive medicines to the treatment actually given; do not take an extra or catch-up anticancer dose yourself.
Follow your oncology unit’s urgent advice for fever, infection, severe diarrhoea, chest pain or difficulty breathing. Bring your treatment card and current medicines list.
Tell both the oncology team and the procedural team that you receive bevacizumab. Holds and restart need an agreed wound-healing plan; do not stop or restart it yourself.
observation_and_access: No ambulatory fluorouracil pump is used in these regimens.
Provide the local stop-and-call pathway and confirm understanding by teach-back.

regimen_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

evidence_at_a_glance.population: AVEX randomised 280 people aged 70 or older with previously untreated metastatic colorectal cancer who were unsuitable for oxaliplatin- or irinotecan-based combinations.
evidence_at_a_glance.comparison: Bevacizumab + capecitabine versus Capecitabine alone
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: In an older population unsuitable for oxaliplatin or irinotecan combinations, adding bevacizumab delayed cancer progression but caused more severe side effects. The capecitabine starting dose in that trial differed from the standard dose in this NCCP regimen. It is not a prediction of your extra lifespan.

endpoints.interpretation: Primary PFS endpoint; older population unsuitable for doublets. Capecitabine 1000 mg/m² BID in the study versus NCCP standard 1250 with lower-start option.
endpoints.analysis_status: Published primary trial or mature follow-up analysis

limitations: In an older population unsuitable for oxaliplatin or irinotecan combinations, adding bevacizumab delayed cancer progression but caused more severe side effects. The capecitabine starting dose in that trial differed from the standard dose in this NCCP regimen. It is not a prediction of your extra lifespan.
Trial results describe groups and cannot predict an individual outcome. The official regimen determines eligibility and dosing.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: AVEX treatment-related grade 3 or worse events: 40% with bevacizumab/capecitabine versus 22% with capecitabine; weigh benefit against toxicity.

evidence_audit.status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
indications_reviewed: Use the exact NCCP indication; DPD testing is a safety assessment, not a tumour biomarker.
For colorectal disease, systemic choices also depend on the MDT plan, disease setting and molecular work-up.

drug_profiles.name: Bevacizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds VEGF, a signal that promotes blood-vessel growth. Blocking VEGF can reduce the blood supply that supports tumour growth; it also affects normal blood vessels and wound healing.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Everolimus
drug_profiles.mechanism: Everolimus binds the intracellular protein FKBP12; this complex inhibits mTORC1, affecting protein synthesis and growth signalling. This pathway can support endocrine resistance, which explains pairing it with an oestrogen-lowering medicine. The same pathway operates in normal tissues, contributing to mouth ulcers, infection risk and metabolic changes.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Exemestane
drug_profiles.mechanism: After menopause, aromatase in tissues converts androgen precursors into oestrogen. Exemestane is an irreversible aromatase inhibitor that reduces this supply to hormone-sensitive cancer cells. It does not directly switch off functioning ovaries; the menopausal indication must be confirmed.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Palbociclib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Your endocrine partner
drug_profiles.drug_type: Either an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant
drug_profiles.drug_class: Either an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant
drug_profiles.mechanism: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant acts at the oestrogen receptor. These are alternative partners here, not an instruction to take both. The partner’s dose, monitoring and injection or tablet schedule must be confirmed.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Ribociclib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Ribociclib blocks CDK4 and CDK6, proteins that help cells move through the cycle of division. Endocrine therapy reduces the hormone signal that can drive HR-positive breast cancer.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: AI or fulvestrant
drug_profiles.mechanism: An aromatase inhibitor (AI) lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant blocks and reduces oestrogen receptors. These are alternative endocrine partners, selected by the team. Ovarian suppression is needed in pre/perimenopausal patients.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Abemaciclib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Abemaciclib inhibits CDK4 and CDK6 proteins. These proteins help cells move towards division. It is combined with endocrine treatment to reduce recurrence risk in eligible high-risk early breast cancer.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Trastuzumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu)
drug_profiles.mechanism: Enhertu links an antibody that recognises HER2 with deruxtecan, a cell-killing medicine. After uptake into the cell, the payload inhibits topoisomerase I and interferes with DNA replication. The released payload can also affect nearby tumour cells. This targeting does not spare every healthy cell, which is why blood counts, nausea, lungs and heart function still need attention.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)
drug_profiles.mechanism: The antibody component recognises Trop-2 on cancer cells. Its linked SN-38 payload interferes with topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in managing DNA during copying, which can damage dividing cells. Healthy tissues can also be affected, particularly blood-forming cells and the gut; being antibody-directed does not mean it is free of chemotherapy-type effects.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Tucatinib
drug_profiles.mechanism: Tucatinib reduces signalling from the internal part of HER2. It works alongside trastuzumab and capecitabine, which act in different ways. Its tablet schedule continues through the capecitabine break.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Capecitabine
drug_profiles.mechanism: The body converts capecitabine into fluorouracil, which disrupts DNA and RNA processes needed for cell growth. Tablets are active chemotherapy; taking them at home still requires a clear monitoring and interruption plan.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Docetaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Doxorubicin is carried inside tiny coated fat particles called liposomes. This changes how it circulates and its side-effect pattern. Heart injury remains possible; skin and mouth effects are especially important.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Paclitaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Eribulin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Eribulin blocks growth of the tiny structures cells need to divide. It can slow cancer growth, but can also affect blood cells and nerves.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Olaparib (Lynparza)
drug_profiles.mechanism: BRCA1 and BRCA2 help cells repair breaks in DNA. Some cancers with these changes rely more heavily on other repair routes. Olaparib inhibits PARP activity and traps PARP on DNA, making it harder for those cancer cells to survive DNA damage. Normal blood-forming cells can also be affected, which is why regular blood counts matter.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Cetuximab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks growth messages. In bowel cancer, a validated RAS wild-type result helps identify whether this approach is suitable. In head-and-neck cancer, weekly cetuximab may be combined with radiotherapy under a separate treatment plan. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Panitumumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: Panitumumab attaches to EGFR, a receptor on the outside of cells. This can interrupt signals that help some bowel cancers grow. A tumour RAS test helps identify whether this approach is suitable. EGFR also supports healthy skin, which explains why skin and nail changes need attention.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Oxaliplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Oxaliplatin makes links within DNA. These interfere with copying and repair, which can stop a cancer cell dividing. Healthy tissues can also be affected.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Folinic acid
drug_profiles.mechanism: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Fluorouracil
drug_profiles.mechanism: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Irinotecan
drug_profiles.mechanism: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Pembrolizumab
drug_profiles.mechanism: PD-1 is a control switch on T cells, a type of immune cell. When it connects with PD-L1 or PD-L2, the T cell receives a signal to reduce its activity. Some cancers use this pathway to escape immune attack. Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, helping T cells recognise and attack the cancer. It does not directly poison cancer cells like chemotherapy. Releasing this brake can also allow immune cells to attack healthy organs, which explains the different side-effect pattern and why symptoms can appear after treatment stops.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Pemetrexed
drug_profiles.mechanism: Pemetrexed is an antifolate: it blocks several enzymes that cells use to turn folate-dependent materials into DNA and RNA building blocks. With fewer building blocks, cancer cells have more difficulty copying their genetic instructions and dividing. Healthy rapidly renewing tissues, including bone marrow and the mouth lining, can also be affected. That helps explain low blood counts and mouth soreness. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce toxicity; they are part of the treatment, not supplements to omit because the drug is an antifolate.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Carboplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Carboplatin is a platinum-containing chemotherapy. Inside cells, it forms chemical attachments to DNA, including links that stop DNA strands working normally. This disrupts copying and repair and can lead to cell death. Healthy cells can also be injured, especially blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. The kidneys help remove carboplatin, so kidney function is used to calculate the dose. AUC 5 describes a target drug exposure over time; it is not a fixed dose of 5 mg.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

drug_profiles.name: Pelvic radiotherapy
drug_profiles.mechanism: Radiation is directed at the planned area. Capecitabine helps sensitise cancer cells to it. Nearby bowel, bladder and skin may also become irritated. Effects can build over the weeks and may continue after the final session.
drug_profiles.review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
